extracted.intended_audience: Sponsors / investigators procuring contract preclinical ADME/PK assays (pharma, biotech, academic groups)
extracted.subtask_description: A commercial study proposal/quotation describing non-GLP ADME, in vitro and in vivo pharmacokinetic assays (CYP inhibition, plasma stability, solubility, permeability, in vivo PK) including procedures, sample requirements, deliverables, turnaround, fees, and contractual terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of isoform‑specific probe substrates and inhibitors (CYP panel)
rubrics_metrics.description: Table 1 lists the inhibitors, substrates, and associated concentrations that will be used for each incubation (isoform-specific probe substrates and inhibitors for multiple CYP isoforms).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform incubations with NADPH-regenerating cofactor solution; include blank solvent and positive controls (isoform-specific inhibitors). Use the listed probe substrates (e.g., phenacetin, bupropion, amodiaquine, diclofenac, S-mephenytoin, dextromethorphan, midazolam) and inhibitors (e.g., fluvoxamine, clopidogrel, quercetin, sulfaphenazole, ticlopidine, quinidine, ketoconazole) at the specified final concentrations (table provides multiple concentration points per inhibitor/substrate).

rubrics_metrics.name: CYP assay incubation times and conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Incubate mixtures at 37°C and 5% CO2 with orbital shaking at 200 rpm for assay-specific times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incubate 5 minutes for reactions containing midazolam, 10 minutes for reactions containing phenacetin, bupropion, diclofenac, or dextromethorphan, and 20 minutes for reactions containing amodiaquine or S-mephenytoin. Quench reactions with acetonitrile containing an internal standard and analyze by LC-MS/MS.

rubrics_metrics.name: CYP activity normalization and IC50 determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Enzyme activity in presence of compounds will be normalized to activity in absence of compounds and expressed as percentage of activity. The inhibitory potential (IC50) will be determined using nonlinear regression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor substrate metabolite formation by LC-MS/MS. Normalize sample activity to control (no compound) and compute percent activity. Fit concentration-response data with nonlinear regression to estimate IC50.

rubrics_metrics.name: CYP assay deliverable format
rubrics_metrics.description: A Microsoft Excel summary report including IC50 summary tables and plots of test compound concentration versus peak area ratios will be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report includes IC50 tables and concentration vs peak-area-ratio plots; delivered as an Excel file.

rubrics_metrics.name: CYP assay turnaround time
rubrics_metrics.description: Report will be delivered within 8 business days from Sponsor’s approval of the study and receipt of all necessary information and assay-specific materials/reagents by Alliance Pharma.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non‑GLP data retention period
rubrics_metrics.description: Data from this non-GLP study will be preserved for 1 year after submission of the results to the Sponsor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to assays described as non-GLP (multiple sections repeat this preservation period).

rubrics_metrics.name: CYP assay fee schedule (per compound pricing basis)
rubrics_metrics.description: The cost of the full-panel CYP inhibition assay is quoted on a per-compound basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Per-compound / per-probe-substrate pricing shown in the Fee Schedule table (document lists Item, Years, Number of compounds, Costs). Exact numeric rates are provided in the quotation/fee schedule pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample information requirements (general for in vitro assays)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsor must provide: molecular weights (formula weights and exact mass units), sufficient amounts of the compounds, stability information (light, temperature, solvents) if available, safety information for handling, and solubility of the compounds if available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This list appears repeatedly (CYP, plasma stability, solubility, MDCK permeability, in vivo PK). Supplying these elements is required to initiate and perform assays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plasma stability study scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the relative stability of compounds in mouse and human plasma.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plasma stability general procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Test compounds will be incubated at a concentration of 1 µM in plasma samples. At 0, 15, 30, 60 and 120 minutes, aliquots will be removed and reactions will be quenched with an acetonitrile solution containing an internal standard. Samples analyzed by LC-MS/MS; results reported as peak area ratios of analyte to internal standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timepoints fixed (0, 15, 30, 60, 120 min) and quench/analyze routine standardized. Use LC-MS/MS and report peak area ratios.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plasma stability deliverables
rubrics_metrics.description: A Microsoft Excel summary report including half-life (t1/2), elimination rate constant, peak area ratios of each analyte to internal standard, and graphic profiles will be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliverable is an Excel file summarizing t1/2, ke, peak area ratios and plots.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plasma stability turnaround time
rubrics_metrics.description: Report will be delivered within 6 business days from Sponsor’s approval of the study and receipt of all necessary information and assay-specific materials/reagents by Alliance Pharma.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plasma stability fee schedule (per compound)
rubrics_metrics.description: The cost of plasma stability analysis is quoted per compound.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fee table lists mouse and human plasma stability items, number of compounds and costs per year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aqueous solubility study scope
rubrics_metrics.description: To assess the solubility of compounds in phosphate-buffered saline (PBS).

rubrics_metrics.name: Aqueous solubility general procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Approximately 1 mL of PBS buffer (pH 7.4) will be added to ~10 mg of each test compound. Solutions sonicated 30 minutes and vortexed at low speed for at least 30 minutes, then sit at room temperature for 16–28 hours. After that, filter through 0.22‑micron filter, followed by dilutions (1:10, 1:100, 1:1000, 1:10,000) in triplicate in 50% acetonitrile in water (1:1, v/v). Final sample solutions mixed with internal standard (1:1) followed by LC-MS/MS analysis. Solubility determined according to calibration curve generated from 5 concentration standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed stepwise protocol including sonication, vortex, incubation time, filtering, serial dilutions in triplicate, internal standard mixing and LC-MS/MS quantitation against 5-point calibration curve.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aqueous solubility deliverables
rubrics_metrics.description: A Microsoft Excel summary report including standard curve information and sample solubility data will be provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aqueous solubility turnaround time
rubrics_metrics.description: Report will be delivered within 7 business days from receipt of compounds by Alliance Pharma.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aqueous solubility sample requirement (mass minimum)
rubrics_metrics.description: Approximately 10 mg of each compound (minimum requirement) should be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also reiterates general sample info (molecular weight, stability, safety, solubility if available).

rubrics_metrics.name: Aqueous solubility fee schedule (per compound)
rubrics_metrics.description: The cost of aqueous solubility analysis is quoted per compound.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fee table identifies number of compounds per year and costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: MDCKII‑MDR1 permeability scope
rubrics_metrics.description: To assess the permeability of compounds in MDCKII-MDR1 cells.

rubrics_metrics.name: MDCK permeability experimental design and QC
rubrics_metrics.description: Permeability assessed in duplicate in both apical→basolateral (A→B) and basolateral→apical (B→A) directions. MDCK cells seeded onto multiwell permeable supports; study conducted ~4 days post-seeding. TEER measured as a quality control for monolayer integrity. Transport medium wash 30 minutes; dosing solution contains Lucifer yellow; incubate at 37°C with 5% CO2; collect apical and basolateral samples for LC-MS/MS. Lucifer yellow fluorometrically determined and serves as in-well quality control for monolayer integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use TEER and Lucifer yellow to monitor monolayer integrity; perform duplicate directional transport assays and analyze samples by LC-MS/MS; maintain incubation conditions and timing as described.

rubrics_metrics.name: MDCK permeability deliverables
rubrics_metrics.description: A spreadsheet summary report (Microsoft Excel file) including the permeability coefficient Papp (B to A) and Papp (A to B) will be provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: MDCK permeability turnaround time
rubrics_metrics.description: The spreadsheet summary report will be delivered within approximately 11 business days from Sponsor’s approval of the study and receipt of all necessary information and assay-specific materials/reagents by Alliance Pharma.

rubrics_metrics.name: MDCK permeability fee schedule (per compound)
rubrics_metrics.description: The cost of MDCKII-MDR1 permeability analysis is quoted per compound.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fee table provides per-compound costs and number of compounds per year.

rubrics_metrics.name: In vivo PK in mice (PO) study scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide in-life animal dosing and sample bioanalysis for pharmacokinetic studies conducted in mice (PO administration).

rubrics_metrics.name: In vivo PO general procedures and sampling
rubrics_metrics.description: One group of 21 mice (n=3 mice per time point) will be administered an oral (PO) dose. Dosing formulation prepared according to Sponsor-provided protocol. Terminal blood plasma samples collected from each animal at 7 established time points within a 24 hour period. Samples analyzed by LC-MS/MS and calculated concentrations reported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design is n=3 per timepoint, 7 timepoints per 24h; Sponsor should provide predicted concentration range/Cmax if available, molecular weight, purity, sufficient standard compound, sample stability and safety info, solubility if available.

rubrics_metrics.name: In vivo PO deliverables
rubrics_metrics.description: A report of abnormal in‑life observations will be provided to the Sponsor if applicable. A Microsoft Excel spreadsheet summary of sample analysis results will be delivered.

rubrics_metrics.name: In vivo PO turnaround time
rubrics_metrics.description: The pharmacokinetic study will be completed and results will be delivered within approximately 10 business days from receipt of the test compound and all other necessary study materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: In vivo PO documentation retention
rubrics_metrics.description: Data from this non-GLP study will be preserved for 1 year after submission of the report to the Sponsor.

rubrics_metrics.name: In vivo PO fee schedule (per compound)
rubrics_metrics.description: The cost of the in vivo pharmacokinetic study (dosing and bioanalysis) is quoted per compound.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fee table lists item, years, number of compounds and costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: In vivo PK in mice (IV/PO) scope and design
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide in-life animal dosing and bioanalysis for PK studies in mice with IV and PO administration using two groups of 21 mice (n=3 per time point).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dosing formulation per Sponsor protocol; terminal plasma samples at 7 time points within 24 hours; LC-MS/MS analysis and concentration reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: In vivo IV/PO deliverables and turnaround
rubrics_metrics.description: A report of abnormal in‑life observations (if applicable) and an Excel spreadsheet summary of sample analysis results will be delivered. Study completed and results delivered within approximately 10 business days from receipt of materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentation retention: non-GLP study data preserved for 1 year after report submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total fee schedule and assay list
rubrics_metrics.description: A consolidated annual fee schedule listing assays including Plasma Protein Binding, Microsomal Clearance, Direct CYP IC50 (3A4 - Testosterone), Direct CYP IC50 (1A2, 2B6, 2C8, 2C9, 2C19, 2D6 and 3A4-Midazolam), Plasma Stability, Aqueous Solubility, Permeability, In Vivo PK in Mice (PO), In Vivo PK in Mice (IV/PO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annual and grand total pricing summarized in the Total Fee Schedule table.

rubrics_metrics.name: Services compliance requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Alliance Pharma shall perform the Services described herein in accordance with (i) this Proposal; (ii) applicable standard operating procedures; (iii) current standards of Good Laboratory Practice/Good Clinical Practice (GLP/GCP) as applicable in the country where the Services are performed; and (iv) any other applicable professional standards, codes, guidelines, laws, rules, and regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performance of Services shall only be initiated after full execution of this Proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mutual non-solicitation clause
rubrics_metrics.description: During the term of this Proposal and for a two (2) year period thereafter, neither party nor its affiliates shall recruit, solicit or induce, or hire any employee of the other party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to direct or indirect recruitment/solicitation/hiring, including employees providing services to Sponsor at the time of hiring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample delivery terms and responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsor shall deliver Chemical and Biological Samples to Alliance Pharma at Sponsor’s risk and expense and at the location identified in the Proposal, along with instructions for handling, storage, and safety requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alliance Pharma will receive shipments only if the equipment required to safely process the samples exists at Alliance Pharma.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restricted use of samples
rubrics_metrics.description: Alliance Pharma shall neither use nor analyze any Chemical or Biological Samples for any purposes other than to perform the Services without Sponsor’s prior written consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Storage and disposal policy for chemical samples
rubrics_metrics.description: Alliance Pharma will store Chemical Samples at appropriate storage conditions as directed by Sponsor for 3 months after submission of the final deliverable and will dispose of the Chemical Samples following the 3-month expiration date unless requested otherwise by Sponsor in writing prior to said date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Storage, return, or destruction policy for biological samples
rubrics_metrics.description: For regulatory (e.g., GLP/GCP) studies, Alliance Pharma will store Biological Samples as directed for 6 months after submission of the final service deliverable. Alliance Pharma will continue to store Biological Samples following the 6-month expiration date at the rate of US $0.50 per Biological Sample per month unless otherwise directed. Sponsor may request destruction, continued storage (at Sponsor expense), or return of samples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For non-regulated studies, Alliance will destroy Biological Samples two weeks after Sponsor acknowledges receipt of final deliverables unless Sponsor requests otherwise in writing prior to that date. An authorization request form will be sent at Sponsor’s request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of biological samples not intended for bioanalysis
rubrics_metrics.description: If Biological Samples are received that are not intended for bioanalysis under the scope of the Proposal (e.g., backup samples), Sponsor will be contacted and offered options to destroy, store under Alliance responsibility, or return to Sponsor at Sponsor’s expense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If stored under Alliance responsibility, such samples (regulatory or non-regulatory) will be stored and invoiced at US $0.50 per Biological Sample per month. Storage fee basis: standard 1.2–2 mL cryogenic vials (max height 49 mm, diameter 13.5 mm); larger containers may incur additional fees to be agreed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Per-sample pricing basis and renegotiation threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Per-sample pricing provided in the Proposal is based on the number of samples requested by the Sponsor. Pricing may be renegotiated if the sample count decreases from the quoted count by more than 20%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If sample count decreases >20%, pricing subject to renegotiation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-assays, repeats, and billing for reanalysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Sample re-assays/repeats requested by Sponsor, dilutional re-assays, and incurred sample reanalysis will be invoiced at the sample unit rate. Re-assays/repeats due to failure to meet the pre-defined criteria will be at no charge to Sponsor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any special requirements from the Sponsor not included in the budget will be invoiced at additional cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pass-through costs and mark-up
rubrics_metrics.description: Pricing includes all standard laboratory consumables; however, the cost of non-standard items (e.g., chromatographic columns, reference standards, internal standards, SPE plates, commercial ELISA kits, enzymes, specific reagents etc.) purchased by Alliance Pharma will be passed-through to the Sponsor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All pass-through costs are subject to a mark-up fee for purchasing, handling and accounting services. Fees may include estimated costs expected at study start; additional materials may be required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Installment invoicing and contract modifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Alliance Pharma will invoice upon delivery of the first draft report for each study. Any additional authorized dollars from contract modifications will be added to the next billing cycle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment terms and late payment penalties
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsor shall pay each invoice within thirty (30) days of receipt. Any overdue amount shall bear interest at a per annum rate of two percent (2%) above the prime rate in effect at Bank of America on the date due. Sponsor shall also pay all reasonable collection costs, including attorneys’ fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any invoice portion is disputed, Sponsor shall pay undisputed amounts and parties shall use good faith efforts to reconcile disputed portion within thirty (30) days of receipt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorization and acceptance of quotation
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitting a purchase order with reference to the quotation number or sending a scanned copy of the signed quotation is considered acceptance of prices and all other special conditions listed on the quotation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This quotation constitutes a separate and distinct contract between Client and Eurofins. In no event shall an affiliate of Eurofins be liable for obligations under the quotation; Client shall look exclusively to Eurofins in relation to rights or remedies under the quotation. Work is subject to MSA or Eurofins General Terms & Conditions of Sale if MSA not active.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order placement and payment methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Orders can be placed by purchase order or credit card. Purchase orders should detail the specified company address. For payments from outside Taiwan, intermediary or sender’s charges should be borne by the sender.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact and address details provided in the quotation; check payment address provided for US remittance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotation validity period
rubrics_metrics.description: This Proposal is valid for sixty (60) calendar days from quotation date.
